passages.text: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.
passages.sermon: The house of Saul and the house of David fought a long war.\r\nDavid became stronger.\r\nThe house of Saul became weaker.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: And sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel; his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur; his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital; and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron.
passages.sermon:
David lived in Hebron.
David had sons in Hebron.
David’s first son was Amnon.
Amnon’s mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel.
David’s second son was Chileab.
Chileab’s mother was Abigail.
Abigail had been the wife of Nabal from Carmel.
David’s third son was Absalom.
Absalom’s mother was Maacah.
Maacah was the daughter of Talmai.
Talmai was the king of Geshur.
David’s fourth son was Adonijah.
Adonijah’s mother was Haggith.
David’s fifth son was Shephatiah.
Shephatiah’s mother was Abital.
David’s sixth son was Ithream.
Ithream’s mother was Eglah.
Eglah was David’s wife.
All these sons were born to David in Hebron.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְדוּ לְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיְהִ֤י בְכוֹרוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן לַאֲחִינֹ֖עַם הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽת׃ וּמִשְׁנֵ֣הוּ כִלְאָ֔ב לַאֲבִיגֵל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֣ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִ֑י וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בֶּֽן־ מַעֲכָ֔ה בַּת־ תַּלְמַ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ גְּשֽׁוּר׃ וְהָרְבִיעִ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּ֣ה בֶן־ חַגִּ֑ית וְהַחֲמִישִׁ֖י שְׁפַטְיָ֥ה בֶן־ אֲבִיטָֽל׃ וְהַשִּׁשִּׁ֣י יִתְרְעָ֔ם לְעֶגְלָ֖ה אֵ֣שֶׁת דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֛לֶּה יֻלְּד֥וּ לְדָוִ֖ד בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃פ

passages.text: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a leader in the house of Saul.
There was a war between the house of Saul and the house of David.
During this war, Abner became stronger in the house of Saul.
Abner increased his power and influence among Saul’s people.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְיוֹת֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וְאַבְנֵ֛ר הָיָ֥ה מִתְחַזֵּ֖ק בְּבֵ֥ית שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”
passages.sermon:
Saul had a concubine.
Her name was Rizpah.
Rizpah was the daughter of Aiah.
Ish-bosheth spoke to Abner.
Ish-bosheth asked Abner a question.
He said, “Why did you go to my father’s concubine?”
passages.original: וּלְשָׁא֣וּל פִּלֶ֔גֶשׁ וּשְׁמָ֖הּ רִצְפָּ֣ה בַת־ אַיָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ אַבְנֵ֔ר מַדּ֥וּעַ בָּ֖אתָה אֶל־ פִּילֶ֥גֶשׁ אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!
passages.sermon:
Abner was a powerful leader in the house of Saul.
Ish-bosheth was Saul’s son.
Ish-bosheth accused Abner of wrongdoing with Saul’s concubine.
Abner became very angry at Ish-bosheth’s words.
Abner spoke to Ish-bosheth.
Abner said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah?”
Abner said, “Today I show kindness to the house of your father Saul.”
Abner said, “I am kind to his brothers and to his friends.”
Abner said, “I have not handed you over to David.”
Abner said, “But today you charge me with a fault concerning this woman.”
passages.original: וַיִּחַר֩ לְאַבְנֵ֨ר מְאֹ֜ד עַל־ דִּבְרֵ֣י אִֽישׁ־ בֹּ֗שֶׁת וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הֲרֹ֨אשׁ כֶּ֥לֶב אָנֹ֘כִי֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָה֒ הַיּ֨וֹם אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ חֶ֜סֶד עִם־ בֵּ֣ית׀ שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֗יךָ אֶל־ אֶחָיו֙ וְאֶל־ מֵ֣רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹ֥א הִמְצִיתִ֖ךָ בְּיַד־ דָּוִ֑ד וַתִּפְקֹ֥ד עָלַ֛י עֲוֺ֥ן הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
passages.sermon:
Abner was a powerful commander in Israel.
Abner spoke with strong words.
Abner said, “May God punish me if I do not act.”
Abner said, “May God punish me even more if I do not do what the LORD promised to David.”
The LORD swore to David that he would be king.
Abner said, “I will take the kingdom away from the house of Saul.”
Abner said, “I will give the kingdom to David.”
Abner said, “I will set up David’s throne over Israel and over Judah.”
Abner said, “David will rule from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.”
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְאַבְנֵ֔ר וְכֹ֖ה יֹסִ֣יף ל֑וֹ כִּ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֔ד כִּֽי־ כֵ֖ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לּֽוֹ׃ לְהַֽעֲבִ֥יר הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה מִבֵּ֣ית שָׁא֑וּל וּלְהָקִ֞ים אֶת־ כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְעַל־ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד־ בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

passages.text: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.
passages.sermon: Ish-bosheth was afraid of Abner.\r\nIsh-bosheth could not answer Abner.\r\nIsh-bosheth did not speak to Abner again.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ יָכֹ֣ל ע֔וֹד לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֖ר דָּבָ֑ר מִיִּרְאָת֖וֹ אֹתֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Then Abner sent messengers in his place to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”
passages.sermon:
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner sent messengers to David.
Abner did not go himself.
The messengers spoke for Abner.
They asked David, “Who owns this land?”
They told David, “Make a covenant with Abner.”
Abner promised to help David.
Abner said, “My hand will be with you.”
Abner promised to bring all Israel to David.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אַבְנֵ֨ר מַלְאָכִ֧ים׀ אֶל־ דָּוִ֛ד תַּחַתוֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר לְמִי־ אָ֑רֶץ לֵאמֹ֗ר כָּרְתָ֤ה בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ אִתִּ֔י וְהִנֵּה֙ יָדִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ לְהָסֵ֥ב אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Judah.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner wanted to make a covenant with David.
David replied to Abner.
David said, “Good.”
David agreed to make a covenant with Abner.
David said, “I will make a covenant with you.”
David required one thing from Abner.
David said, “There is one thing I ask from you.”
David said, “Do not come to see me unless you bring Michal.”
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
David said, “You must bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, when you come to see me.”
David said, “If you do not bring Michal, you will not see my face.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ט֔וֹב אֲנִ֕י אֶכְרֹ֥ת אִתְּךָ֖ בְּרִ֑ית אַ֣ךְ דָּבָ֣ר אֶחָ֡ד אָנֹכִי֩ שֹׁאֵ֨ל מֵאִתְּךָ֤ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא־ תִרְאֶ֣ה אֶת־ פָּנַ֔י כִּ֣י׀ אִם־ לִפְנֵ֣י הֱבִיאֲךָ֗ אֵ֚ת מִיכַ֣ל בַּת־ שָׁא֔וּל בְּבֹאֲךָ֖ לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־ פָּנָֽי׃ס

passages.text: Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Judah.
Ish-bosheth was the son of Saul.
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
David had married Michal.
David had paid a bride price for Michal.
He gave one hundred Philistine foreskins for her.
David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth.
David told them what to say.
He said, “Give me back my wife Michal.”
He said, “I betrothed her to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ אִֽישׁ־ בֹּ֥שֶׁת בֶּן־ שָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹ֑ר תְּנָ֤ה אֶת־ אִשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־ מִיכַ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵרַ֣שְׂתִּי לִ֔י בְּמֵאָ֖ה עָרְל֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.
passages.sermon:
Ish-bosheth was the son of Saul.
Ish-bosheth sent messengers.
The messengers took Michal.
Michal was with her husband.
Her husband was Paltiel.
Paltiel was the son of Laish.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אִ֣ישׁ בֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיִּקָּחֶ֖הָ מֵ֣עִֽם אִ֑ישׁ מֵעִ֖ם פַּלְטִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־ לוּשׁ׃

passages.text: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.
passages.sermon:
Michal was the wife of Paltiel son of Laish.
David demanded that Michal be returned to him.
Ish-bosheth took Michal from her husband Paltiel.
Paltiel followed Michal as she was taken away.
Paltiel walked behind Michal.
Paltiel wept as he followed her.
Paltiel followed her all the way to Bahurim.
Abner spoke to Paltiel.
Abner said, “Go back.”
Paltiel returned home.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אִתָּ֜הּ אִישָׁ֗הּ הָל֧וֹךְ וּבָכֹ֛ה אַחֲרֶ֖יהָ עַד־ בַּֽחֻרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו אַבְנֵ֛ר לֵ֥ךְ שׁ֖וּב וַיָּשֹֽׁב׃

passages.text: Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a commander in Israel.
Abner spoke with the elders of Israel.
Abner said to them, “You wanted David to be your king in the past.
You wanted this not only yesterday, but also the day before.
You have been seeking David as king over you.”
passages.original: וּדְבַר־ אַבְנֵ֣ר הָיָ֔ה עִם־ זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר גַּם־ תְּמוֹל֙ גַּם־ שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם הֱיִיתֶ֞ם מְבַקְשִׁ֧ים אֶת־ דָּוִ֛ד לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now take action, because the LORD has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Abner spoke to the elders of Israel.
Abner told them to act now.
The LORD spoke to David.
The LORD called David His servant.
The LORD said He would save His people Israel through David.
The LORD promised to rescue Israel from the Philistines.
The LORD also promised to save Israel from all their enemies.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה עֲשׂ֑וּ כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אָמַ֤ר אֶל־ דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּיַ֣ד׀ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֗י הוֹשִׁ֜יעַ אֶת־ עַמִּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִיַּ֖ד כָּל־ אֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites and went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a commander in Israel.
Abner spoke to the tribe of Benjamin.
Abner told them important things.
Abner then went to Hebron.
Abner spoke to David in Hebron.
Abner told David everything that seemed good to Israel.
Abner also told David what seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר גַּם־ אַבְנֵ֖ר בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גַּם־ אַבְנֵ֗ר לְדַבֵּ֞ר בְּאָזְנֵ֤י דָוִד֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן אֵ֤ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ טוֹב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

passages.text: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a commander in Israel.
Abner came to David.
David was in Hebron.
Twenty men came with Abner.
David welcomed Abner and his men.
David prepared a feast for Abner and his men.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א אַבְנֵ֤ר אֶל־ דָּוִד֙ חֶבְר֔וֹן וְאִתּ֖וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַשׂ דָּוִ֧ד לְאַבְנֵ֛ר וְלַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.” So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace.
passages.sermon:
Abner spoke to David.
Abner said, “Let me go now.”
Abner said, “I will gather all Israel to you, my lord the king.”
Abner said, “They will make a covenant with you.”
Abner said, “You will rule over everything your heart desires.”
David sent Abner away.
Abner left in peace.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְנֵ֣ר אֶל־ דָּוִ֡ד אָק֣וּמָה׀ וְֽאֵלֵ֡כָה וְאֶקְבְּצָה֩ אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִכְרְת֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּרִ֔ית וּמָ֣לַכְתָּ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיְּשַׁלַּ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֖ר וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron because David had sent him on his way in peace.
passages.sermon:
David was king in Hebron.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid.
They brought back much plunder.
Abner was not with David in Hebron.
David had sent Abner away.
Abner left in peace.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֩ עַבְדֵ֨י דָוִ֤ד וְיוֹאָב֙ בָּ֣א מֵֽהַגְּד֔וּד וְשָׁלָ֥ל רָ֖ב עִמָּ֣ם הֵבִ֑יאוּ וְאַבְנֵ֗ר אֵינֶ֤נּוּ עִם־ דָּוִד֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י שִׁלְּח֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander of David’s army.
Joab arrived with all his troops.
Someone told Joab important news.
They said, “Abner son of Ner came to the king.”
They also said, “The king sent Abner away in peace.”
passages.original: וְיוֹאָ֛ב וְכָל־ הַצָּבָ֥א אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ בָּ֑אוּ וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְיוֹאָב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּֽא־ אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־ נֵר֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֖הוּ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab went to King David.
Joab spoke to the king.
Joab said, “What have you done?”
Joab said, “Abner came to you.”
Joab said, “Why did you send Abner away?”
Joab said, “Now Abner is leaving.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָה הִנֵּה־ בָ֤א אַבְנֵר֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ לָמָּה־ זֶּ֥ה שִׁלַּחְתּ֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ הָלֽוֹךְ׃

passages.text: Surely you realize that Abner son of Ner came to deceive you and to track your movements and all that you are doing.”
passages.sermon:
Joab spoke to King David.
Joab warned David about Abner son of Ner.
Joab said Abner came to deceive David.
Joab said Abner wanted to know where David goes out and comes in.
Joab said Abner wanted to learn everything David does.
passages.original: יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־ נֵ֔ר כִּ֥י לְפַתֹּתְךָ֖ בָּ֑א וְלָדַ֜עַת אֶת־ מוֹצָֽאֲךָ֙ וְאֶת־ מְבוֹאֶךָ וְלָדַ֕עַת אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: As soon as Joab had left David, he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David was unaware of it.
passages.sermon:
Joab left David.
Joab sent messengers after Abner.
The messengers brought Abner back from the well of Sirah.
David did not know about this.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹאָב֙ מֵעִ֣ם דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ מִבּ֣וֹר הַסִּרָ֑ה וְדָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃

passages.text: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately, and there Joab stabbed him in the stomach. So Abner died on account of the blood of Joab’s brother Asahel.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a military leader.
He was the son of Ner.
Abner returned to the city of Hebron.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab met Abner at the gate of Hebron.
Joab pulled Abner aside into the gateway.
Joab acted as if he wanted to speak with Abner privately.
Joab stabbed Abner in the stomach.
Abner died there.
Joab killed Abner because Abner had killed Joab’s brother Asahel.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שָׁב אַבְנֵר֙ חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיַּטֵּ֤הוּ יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־ תּ֣וֹךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר לְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּשֶּׁ֑לִי וַיַּכֵּ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ הַחֹ֔מֶשׁ וַיָּ֕מָת בְּדַ֖ם עֲשָׂה־ אֵ֥ל אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: Afterward, David heard about this and said, “I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before the LORD concerning the blood of Abner son of Ner.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Joab killed Abner, the son of Ner.
David did not know about this before it happened.
Afterward, David heard about Abner’s death.
David spoke to the people.
David said, “I am not guilty before the LORD for the blood of Abner son of Ner.
My kingdom is also not guilty before the LORD forever for Abner’s blood.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע דָּוִד֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָקִ֨י אָנֹכִ֧י וּמַמְלַכְתִּ֛י מֵעִ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם מִדְּמֵ֖י אַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־ נֵֽר׃

passages.text: May it whirl over the heads of Joab and the entire house of his father, and may the house of Joab never be without one having a discharge or skin disease, or one who leans on a staff or falls by the sword or lacks food.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke about Joab and Joab’s family.
David said, “Let this trouble come upon Joab’s head.
Let it come upon all his father’s house.
Let the house of Joab never be without someone who has a discharge.
Let the house of Joab never be without someone who has a skin disease.
Let the house of Joab never be without someone who uses a staff to walk.
Let the house of Joab never be without someone who dies by the sword.
Let the house of Joab never be without someone who lacks food.”
passages.original: יָחֻ֙לוּ֙ עַל־ רֹ֣אשׁ יוֹאָ֔ב וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יו וְֽאַל־ יִכָּרֵ֣ת מִבֵּ֣ית יוֹאָ֡ב זָ֠ב וּמְצֹרָ֞ע וּמַחֲזִ֥יק בַּפֶּ֛לֶךְ וְנֹפֵ֥ל בַּחֶ֖רֶב וַחֲסַר־ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.)
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in David’s army.
Abishai was Joab’s brother.
Abner was a commander in Saul’s army.
Joab and Abishai killed Abner.
Abner had killed Asahel.
Asahel was the brother of Joab and Abishai.
Abner killed Asahel during the battle at Gibeon.
passages.original: וְיוֹאָב֙ וַאֲבִישַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו הָרְג֖וּ לְאַבְנֵ֑ר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵמִ֜ית אֶת־ עֲשָׂהאֵ֧ל אֲחִיהֶ֛ם בְּגִבְע֖וֹן בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then David ordered Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David himself walked behind the funeral bier.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Joab.
King David spoke to all the people with Joab.
David gave them a command.
He said, “Tear your clothes.”
He said, “Put on sackcloth.”
He said, “Mourn before Abner.”
King David walked behind Abner’s funeral bier.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־ יוֹאָ֜ב וְאֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֗וֹ קִרְע֤וּ בִגְדֵיכֶם֙ וְחִגְר֣וּ שַׂקִּ֔ים וְסִפְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֑ר וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד הֹלֵ֖ךְ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַמִּטָּֽה׃

passages.text: When they buried Abner in Hebron, the king wept aloud at Abner’s tomb, and all the people wept.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a military leader in Israel.
People buried Abner in Hebron.
King David was present at the burial.
King David raised his voice and wept at Abner’s tomb.
All the people also wept for Abner.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֖ר בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיִשָּׂ֧א הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֶת־ קוֹל֗וֹ וַיֵּבְךְּ֙ אֶל־ קֶ֣בֶר אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיִּבְכּ֖וּ כָּל־ הָעָֽם׃פ

passages.text: And the king sang this lament for Abner: “Should Abner die the death of a fool?
passages.sermon: King David sang a lament for Abner.\r\nDavid spoke about Abner’s death.\r\nDavid asked, “Should Abner die like a fool?”
passages.original: וַיְקֹנֵ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ אַבְנֵ֖ר וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַכְּמ֥וֹת נָבָ֖ל יָמ֥וּת אַבְנֵֽר׃

passages.text: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered. As a man falls before the wicked, so also you fell.” And all the people wept over him even more.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a commander in Israel.
Abner died in Hebron.
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke at Abner’s burial.
David said, “Your hands were not tied.”
David said, “Your feet were not chained.”
David said, “You fell as a man falls before wicked people.”
All the people wept for Abner even more.
passages.original: יָדֶ֣ךָ לֹֽא־ אֲסֻר֗וֹת וְרַגְלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֹא־ לִנְחֻשְׁתַּ֣יִם הֻגָּ֔שׁוּ כִּנְפ֛וֹל לִפְנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־ עַוְלָ֖ה נָפָ֑לְתָּ וַיֹּסִ֥פוּ כָל־ הָעָ֖ם לִבְכּ֥וֹת עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then all the people came and urged David to eat something while it was still day, but David took an oath, saying, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!”
passages.sermon:
All the people came to David.
They urged David to eat bread while it was still day.
David was the king of Israel.
David took an oath.
David said, “May God punish me, and punish me even more, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א כָל־ הָעָ֗ם לְהַבְר֧וֹת אֶת־ דָּוִ֛ד לֶ֖חֶם בְּע֣וֹד הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע דָּוִ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י אִם־ לִפְנֵ֧י בֽוֹא־ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ אֶטְעַם־ לֶ֖חֶם א֥וֹ כָל־ מְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: All the people took note and were pleased. In fact, everything the king did pleased them.
passages.sermon:
All the people saw what happened.
All the people understood it.
The people were pleased.
Everything the king did pleased all the people.
passages.original: וְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם הִכִּ֔ירוּ וַיִּיטַ֖ב בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּעֵינֵ֥י כָל־ הָעָ֖ם טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: So on that day all the troops and all Israel were convinced that the king had no part in the murder of Abner son of Ner.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Abner son of Ner had been killed.
On that day, all the people understood something important.
All Israel also understood this.
They knew the king did not order the death of Abner.
They saw that David had no part in killing Abner.
passages.original: וַיֵּדְע֧וּ כָל־ הָעָ֛ם וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הָיְתָה֙ מֵֽהַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהָמִ֖ית אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־ נֵֽר׃פ

passages.text: Then the king said to his servants, “Do you not realize that a great prince has fallen today in Israel?
passages.sermon: David was the king of Israel.\r\nDavid spoke to his servants.\r\nDavid said, “A great leader has died today in Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֑יו הֲל֣וֹא תֵדְע֔וּ כִּי־ שַׂ֣ר וְגָד֗וֹל נָפַ֛ל הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And I am weak this day, though anointed as king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too fierce for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil!”
passages.sermon:
David was king on that day.
God had anointed David as king.
David felt weak.
The sons of Zeruiah were men in Israel.
The sons of Zeruiah were stronger than David.
The sons of Zeruiah were too fierce for David.
David asked the LORD to repay the evildoer.
David wanted the LORD to repay each evildoer for his evil.
passages.original: וְאָנֹכִ֨י הַיּ֥וֹם רַךְ֙ וּמָשׁ֣וּחַ מֶ֔לֶךְ וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָאֵ֛לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י צְרוּיָ֖ה קָשִׁ֣ים מִמֶּ֑נִּי יְשַׁלֵּ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה לְעֹשֵׂ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה כְּרָעָתֽוֹ׃פ
